intent.raw_query: Iceland Northern Lights and hot springs, $3500 couple, January

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunting Tour
experiences.description: Join a guided evening tour away from Reykjavik's light pollution to witness the Aurora Borealis dancing across the sky. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and you'll learn about the science behind this natural phenomenon while capturing stunning photographs.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, silica mud masks, and steam caves while surrounded by dramatic lava fields. Book the Comfort package for access to the lagoon, a silica mud mask, and a drink at the in-water bar.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring dating back to 1891 surrounded by geothermal activity, bubbling geysers, and a small waterfall. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic experience offers a more intimate connection with Iceland's geothermal landscape.

experiences.name: Vatnajökull Glacier Hike
experiences.description: Strap on crampons and explore the largest glacier in Europe with a certified glacier guide. Trek across stunning ice formations, peer into brilliant blue crevasses, and learn about Iceland's rapidly changing glacial landscape. This guided hike offers an unforgettable encounter with Iceland's raw natural power.

experiences.name: Landmannalaugar Highland Hot Springs Trek
experiences.description: Hike through Iceland's surreal rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains in the Highlands and reward yourself with a soak in natural geothermal hot springs at the base camp. The vivid landscape of red, green, yellow, and purple volcanic rock is unlike anywhere else on Earth, making this a bucket-list nature experience.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Iceland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 06:10. Clear customs and collect luggage. Take the Flybus or a budget shuttle to Reykjavik BSI terminal, then arrange onward travel north toward Siglufjörður. The drive is approximately 4-5 hours via Route 1 and the Héðinsfjörður tunnel. Rest and recover from the flight during the journey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Siglufjörður in the early afternoon. Check in early if possible at Hotel Siglunes on Lækjargata 10, or store luggage and take a gentle walk along the harbour front to get oriented. Siglufjörður is a charming small fishing town nestled in a dramatic fjord — explore the colourful wooden houses and the quiet harbour area.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into the hotel and rest after the long travel day. As darkness falls (which comes early in January), step outside or find a dark spot near the harbour to watch for the Northern Lights — January skies in northern Iceland offer excellent aurora opportunities. Dress in all your warmest layers.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or coffee at Keflavik Airport before departure — budget around 1,000–1,500 ISK for a pastry and coffee.
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches or snacks from a Reykjavik Bonus or Krónan supermarket before heading north to save money on the road.
meals.dinner: Visit Hannes Boy restaurant in Siglufjörður for a local meal — try the fish soup, a hearty and affordable Icelandic staple (around 2,500–3,500 ISK).

day_by_day.notes: January days in Siglufjörður are very short — expect only 4–5 hours of daylight. The road north can be icy and subject to closures; check road.is before driving. Consider renting a 4WD vehicle for safety. Budget tip: buy groceries at a Reykjavik supermarket (Bonus or Krónan) before leaving the capital as prices are significantly lower than in small towns.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið) in Siglufjörður, one of Iceland's most acclaimed regional museums. It tells the fascinating story of the town's herring boom in the early 20th century through restored buildings and exhibits. Entry is around 2,000 ISK — well worth it for a budget-friendly cultural morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a scenic walk along the fjord shoreline toward the old fish factory ruins at the edge of town. The surrounding mountains draped in snow create a stunning backdrop. If weather permits, hike a short distance up the lower slopes above town for panoramic views of the fjord below.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights watch from the harbour or the hillside above town. Siglufjörður's remote location means very little light pollution — ideal aurora viewing conditions. Download the Vedur aurora forecast app and the Icelandic Met Office app to track activity. Bring a thermos of hot chocolate.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered breakfast at the hotel using groceries purchased in Reykjavik — oats, yogurt, bread, and coffee (budget 500–800 ISK).
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from hotel room — bread, cheese, and local skyr from the small local shop in Siglufjörður.
meals.dinner: Cook a simple pasta or soup dinner in the hotel kitchen if available, or visit the local Við Árholt grill for a budget burger or hot dog (around 1,500–2,000 ISK).

day_by_day.notes: The Herring Era Museum may have reduced winter hours — call ahead or check online. Wear microspike traction devices on shoes for icy paths. The Northern Lights are most active between 10 PM and 2 AM; set an alarm and check the forecast before bed.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south along Route 76 through the dramatic Héðinsfjörður tunnel and along the coast toward Hofsós, a tiny village on the Skagafjörður fjord. The drive itself is spectacular with snow-covered mountains plunging into the sea. Stop at any scenic viewpoints along the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Hofsós Infinity Pool — a geothermally heated outdoor swimming pool perched dramatically on the edge of the fjord with views across to the mountains. Entry is approximately 1,000–1,200 ISK, making it one of Iceland's most affordable and visually stunning hot spring experiences. Soak for as long as you like.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður before dark (around 4–5 PM). Spend the evening aurora hunting from the hillside above town or along the quiet road east of the harbour. The clear winter nights in this region are among the best in Iceland for Northern Lights viewing.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel — eggs, toast, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Pack a thermos of soup and sandwiches to enjoy at the Hofsós pool area or in the car with fjord views.
meals.dinner: Hannes Boy in Siglufjörður — try the lamb soup or fish of the day for a warming, budget-friendly meal (2,500–3,500 ISK).

day_by_day.notes: The drive to Hofsós is approximately 45 minutes each way. Road conditions in January can be challenging — always check road.is before departing. The Hofsós pool is one of Iceland's hidden gems and far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon at a fraction of the price. Bring a towel and swimsuit.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Siglufjörður valley on foot. Follow the river path inland from the town toward the head of the fjord where the valley narrows dramatically between steep avalanche-prone slopes. The scenery is raw and powerful in winter. Look for Arctic birds such as ptarmigan and redwings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive through the Strákagöng tunnel to the neighbouring village of Ólafsfjörður (about 20 minutes). Walk around this equally charming small fishing village, visit the local swimming pool (Sundlaug Ólafsfjarðar) for a warm soak — entry around 900–1,100 ISK. The pool has hot pots and is used by locals.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður. Spend the evening in the hotel common area with a warm drink, planning the next days of the trip. If aurora activity is forecast, head out after 9 PM for a dedicated Northern Lights watch from the dark hillside above town.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — skyr with granola and fruit, coffee.
meals.lunch: Visit the small bakery or café in Ólafsfjörður for a soup and bread lunch (around 1,500–2,000 ISK).
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner at hotel — cook a simple Icelandic lamb stew using ingredients from the local shop (budget 1,500–2,000 ISK for ingredients).

day_by_day.notes: The valley walk at the head of Siglufjörður is not a marked trail in winter — stay on the flat valley floor and do not approach the steep slopes due to avalanche risk. Ólafsfjörður's swimming pool is a wonderful authentic local experience. January is the quietest tourist month in this region — you may have the pool almost entirely to yourself.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip east along Route 76 toward Sauðárkrókur, the largest town in the Skagafjörður region (about 1 hour drive). Stop at the Glaumbær turf farm museum along the way — one of Iceland's best-preserved historic turf farmsteads, offering a glimpse into traditional Icelandic rural life. Entry around 1,800 ISK.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue into Sauðárkrókur for a walk around the town. Visit the local swimming pool (Sundlaug Sauðárkróks) which has excellent hot pots and a waterslide — entry around 1,000 ISK. Stock up on groceries at the local supermarket (Krónan or Nettó) to replenish supplies at a lower cost than Siglufjörður.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Siglufjörður via the scenic coastal road. Stop at a dark roadside pullout on the return journey for Northern Lights viewing if the forecast is active. The open landscape between Sauðárkrókur and the fjords offers wide sky views ideal for aurora watching.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel.
meals.lunch: Grab a budget meal at a petrol station grill in Sauðárkrókur — Icelandic hot dogs (pylsur) are a national institution and cost only 500–700 ISK each.
meals.dinner: Self-catered using fresh groceries purchased in Sauðárkrókur — grilled fish or lamb with vegetables (budget 1,500–2,000 ISK).

day_by_day.notes: Glaumbær may have limited winter opening hours — check ahead. Sauðárkrókur is the best place in the region to stock up on affordable groceries. The Icelandic hot dog (pylsa) with all the toppings — remoulade, raw onion, crispy onion, ketchup, and mustard — is a must-try budget food experience.

day_by_day.morning: Take a slow morning in Siglufjörður. Walk the full length of the harbour in the early light (sunrise is around 11 AM in January at this latitude). Photograph the colourful fishing boats against the snow-covered mountains. Visit the small local church, Siglufjörðarkirkja, which dates to 1932.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive west along Route 76 toward Skagaströnd on the Skagi peninsula (about 1.5 hours). The Skagi peninsula is one of Iceland's least-visited areas and offers dramatic coastal scenery, sea cliffs, and excellent birdwatching. Walk along the black sand beach at Kálfshamarsvík with its striking basalt columns.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður. This is a good evening to try the local swimming pool (Sundlaug Siglufjarðar) — a geothermally heated pool with hot pots, very popular with locals. Entry around 900–1,100 ISK. Afterward, Northern Lights watch from the harbour.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — eggs, toast, skyr.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Kálfshamarsvík with views of the basalt columns and sea.
meals.dinner: Hannes Boy restaurant — fish and chips or the catch of the day (2,500–3,500 ISK).

day_by_day.notes: The Skagi peninsula road can be icy and remote in January — ensure the car has a full tank and emergency supplies. Kálfshamarsvík basalt columns are a lesser-known gem comparable to Reynisfjara but without the crowds. The local swimming pool in Siglufjörður is a wonderful way to meet locals and warm up after a cold day.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day. Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely self-catered breakfast. Spend the morning reading, journaling, or exploring the small streets and back lanes of Siglufjörður that you may have missed. Visit the small local art gallery or craft shop if open.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive back through the Héðinsfjörður tunnel to Ólafsfjörður and continue east along Route 82 toward Dalvík (about 1 hour from Siglufjörður). Dalvík is a small fishing town with a charming local museum, Byggðasafnið Hvoll, which features a famous exhibit on the tallest man in Icelandic history. Entry is free or by donation.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður. Dedicated Northern Lights evening — drive 5–10 minutes out of town on the road toward Héðinsfjörður for a completely dark sky. Bring a tripod if you have a camera for long-exposure aurora photography. Stay out until midnight if activity is high.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely self-catered breakfast — pancakes or French toast with jam.
meals.lunch: Visit the Dalvík harbour area for a simple fish soup at a local café (around 1,500–2,000 ISK).
meals.dinner: Self-catered at hotel — pasta with a tomato and lamb sauce using local minced lamb (budget 1,200–1,800 ISK).

day_by_day.notes: A rest day mid-trip is important, especially in challenging winter conditions. The drive to Dalvík passes through beautiful fjord scenery. Dalvík is also the departure point for whale watching tours in summer, but in January the focus is on the town's cosy winter atmosphere. Check aurora forecast before the evening outing.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Siglufjörður to Akureyri, Iceland's second-largest city (about 1.5 hours via Route 82 through Dalvík and along the Eyjafjörður fjord). Arrive in Akureyri and walk the main shopping street, Hafnarstræti. Visit the iconic Akureyrarkirkja church perched on the hill above the town — free entry and stunning views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Akureyri Botanical Garden (Lystigarðurinn) — even in January the garden is a peaceful snowy landscape and entry is free. Explore the old town area with its well-preserved early 20th-century wooden houses. Visit the Akureyri Art Museum (Listasafnið á Akureyri) for a budget-friendly cultural experience (around 1,500 ISK).
day_by_day.evening: Soak at the Akureyri Swimming Pool (Sundlaug Akureyrar) — one of the best municipal pools in Iceland with multiple hot pots, a steam room, and a waterslide. Entry around 1,000–1,200 ISK. Afterward, find a dark spot on the outskirts of Akureyri for Northern Lights viewing before the drive back to Siglufjörður.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast before departure.
meals.lunch: Visit Bræðraborg café in Akureyri for a budget soup and bread lunch (around 1,800–2,500 ISK) — a local favourite.
meals.dinner: Grab a budget meal at Akureyri's Noodle Station (around 1,500–2,000 ISK) for a warming Asian noodle soup before the drive back, or pick up groceries from Bonus supermarket in Akureyri.

day_by_day.notes: Akureyri is the cultural and commercial hub of northern Iceland. The Bonus supermarket in Akureyri is one of the best places to stock up on affordable groceries in the north. The drive back to Siglufjörður along the Eyjafjörður fjord at night can be magical if the Northern Lights are active over the water.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Siglufjörður to the Mývatn lake area (about 2 hours via Akureyri and Route 1 east). Mývatn is one of Iceland's most geologically active and visually dramatic regions. Begin with a walk around the Skútustaðagígar pseudo-craters on the south shore of the lake — a surreal volcanic landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Mývatn Nature Baths (Jarðböðin við Mývatn) — a geothermal lagoon similar to the Blue Lagoon but far less expensive and less crowded. Entry is approximately 5,500–6,500 ISK, making it a splurge for a budget trip but far cheaper than the Blue Lagoon. Soak in the milky blue mineral-rich waters surrounded by volcanic steam and winter scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Drive to the Hverir geothermal area near Námafjall for a free and dramatic evening experience — bubbling mud pools and steaming fumaroles create an otherworldly atmosphere. Then find a dark spot near the lake for Northern Lights viewing before the drive back to Siglufjörður.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast before the long drive.
meals.lunch: Pack a substantial lunch from the hotel to eat at the Skútustaðagígar crater area.
meals.dinner: Gamli Bærinn restaurant near Mývatn for a budget lamb soup or fish dish (2,500–3,500 ISK) before the drive back, or self-catered back at the hotel.

day_by_day.notes: This is a long day with significant driving — approximately 4 hours total. Start early to maximise the limited daylight hours. The Mývatn Nature Baths are a highlight of any Iceland trip and worth the budget splurge. Hverir is free and open at all hours. The road back to Siglufjörður via Akureyri is well-maintained but check road.is for conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the immediate surroundings of Siglufjörður more deeply. Walk the road that continues east of town past the old avalanche barriers toward the end of the accessible valley. The scale of the mountains above the town is most apparent from this direction. Look for snow buntings and other winter birds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Siglufjörður Folk Music Centre (Þjóðlagasetur) if open — it celebrates Iceland's traditional folk music heritage. Spend the afternoon in the hotel common area learning about Icelandic culture, language basics, and planning the final days of the trip. Visit the local swimming pool for a warm afternoon soak.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights photography session. Set up on the harbour pier or the hillside above town. The reflection of the aurora in the calm fjord waters can create spectacular images. Stay out as long as the forecast and temperature allow.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — oatmeal with honey and dried fruit.
meals.lunch: Self-catered packed lunch eaten during the valley walk.
meals.dinner: Hannes Boy restaurant — try the traditional Icelandic lamb dish or the fresh Arctic char (2,500–3,500 ISK).

day_by_day.notes: January 25th is approaching the end of the trip — use this quieter day to rest, reflect, and enjoy the unique atmosphere of Siglufjörður in deep winter. The town has a special melancholy beauty in January that is quite different from the summer tourist season. The folk music centre celebrates the kvæðaskapur tradition of Icelandic ballad singing.

day_by_day.morning: Final major day trip — drive to the Tröllaskagi peninsula between Siglufjörður and Akureyri. Take the scenic mountain road (Route 82) over the Ólafsfjarðarmúli pass if conditions allow, or through the tunnels. Stop at the Árskógssandur ferry terminal area and walk along the coast with views across Eyjafjörður.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the small village of Hjalteyri on the inner Eyjafjörður fjord — a former whale processing station now home to an art gallery and cultural space. The industrial ruins and fjord setting are hauntingly beautiful in winter. Continue to Dalvík for a final visit to the local swimming pool.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður for a final Northern Lights watch. This is the last full night in the north — make the most of the dark skies. Drive to the Héðinsfjörður tunnel entrance for a completely unobstructed view of the northern sky.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — a hearty breakfast before the day trip.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Hjalteyri with views of the fjord.
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at Hannes Boy — treat yourself to the full fish course or the lamb fillet as a trip highlight meal (3,000–4,500 ISK).

day_by_day.notes: The mountain road over Ólafsfjarðarmúli is only passable in good winter conditions — check road.is carefully. The Hjalteyri whale station is a fascinating piece of Icelandic industrial history. This is the penultimate full day in Siglufjörður — savour the unique atmosphere of this remote northern town.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Siglufjörður. Take a slow farewell walk around the harbour and town. Visit any spots you want to see one last time. Pack bags and check out of Hotel Siglunes. Begin the drive south toward Reykjavik (approximately 5–6 hours via Route 1).
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at Varmahlíð in the Skagafjörður valley for a break and a visit to the Skagafjörður Heritage Museum (Héraðssafn Skagafjarðar) if time allows. Continue south through the dramatic Holtavörðuheiði highland plateau — a vast, windswept lava and moorland landscape that feels like the edge of the world in winter.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Reykjavik in the early evening. Check into a budget guesthouse or hostel (Kex Hostel, Loft Hostel, or Bus Hostel are all good budget options at 4,000–7,000 ISK per night for a dorm or basic room). Take an evening walk along the Reykjavik waterfront and Harpa Concert Hall.

meals.breakfast: Final self-catered breakfast at Hotel Siglunes — use up remaining food supplies.
meals.lunch: Stop at a petrol station in Varmahlíð or Blönduós for a hot dog and coffee (budget 800–1,200 ISK).
meals.dinner: In Reykjavik, visit Hlöllabátar (Subway-style sandwich shop) or Noodle Station for an affordable dinner (1,500–2,500 ISK).

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Siglufjörður to Reykjavik in January requires careful planning — check road.is for the Holtavörðuheiði plateau conditions as this section can close in severe weather. Allow extra time and do not rush. Arriving in Reykjavik gives you access to a wider range of budget dining and accommodation options for the final night.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Reykjavik. Visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church (free to enter the church; tower viewing costs 1,000 ISK) for panoramic views over the city. Walk down Skólavörðustígur street with its colourful shops and cafés. Visit the Reykjavik Flea Market (Kolaportið) if it is open on weekends for affordable Icelandic souvenirs and local food.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Reykjavik City Thermal Pool (Sundhöll Reykjavíkur) — the oldest pool in the city, recently renovated, with beautiful hot pots. Entry around 1,000–1,200 ISK. A perfect final Icelandic hot spring experience. Afterward, head to the airport area — the Flybus departs from BSI terminal and takes 45 minutes to Keflavik Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Keflavik International Airport. Arrive at the airport at least 2.5 hours before your flight. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days in Iceland's remote north — the Northern Lights, the hot springs, the dramatic fjords, and the unique character of Siglufjörður.

meals.breakfast: Visit Brauð & Co bakery in Reykjavik for fresh Icelandic cinnamon rolls and coffee — a beloved local institution (around 1,200–1,800 ISK).
meals.lunch: Grab a final Icelandic hot dog at the famous Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur hot dog stand near the harbour (500–700 ISK) — a Reykjavik institution since 1937.
meals.dinner: Airport meal at Keflavik — budget 2,000–3,000 ISK for a meal at the airport restaurants, or bring snacks from the city.

day_by_day.notes: Kolaportið flea market is only open on weekends (Saturday and Sunday) — check if the date falls on a weekend. The Flybus must be booked in advance at flybus.is. Allow plenty of time for the airport as Keflavik can be busy even in January. Final budget tip: return any remaining Icelandic króna at the airport exchange or use them on duty-free Icelandic products like skyr, Brennivín, or Icelandic chocolate as souvenirs.

trip_options.title: Classic Iceland Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Keflavik International Airport at 06:10. Clear customs and collect luggage. Take the Flybus or rent a car for the long drive north to Siglufjörður (approx. 5–6 hours). Stop in Reykjavik briefly for supplies and breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the scenic drive north via Route 1 and then Route 76 through the Tröllaskagi peninsula. Arrive in Siglufjörður in the early afternoon. Check in to Hotel Siglunes, freshen up, and take a gentle stroll around the charming harbor town to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Rest and recover from travel. Step outside after dark to scan the sky for the Northern Lights from the hotel or nearby harbor — Siglufjörður's low light pollution makes it an excellent spot. Bundle up warmly.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick bite at a café near Keflavik or Reykjavik before the drive north — try Kaffi Duus in Keflavik for a warm soup or pastry (approx. 1,500–2,000 ISK).
meals.lunch: Pack snacks and sandwiches from a Bonus or Krónan supermarket in Reykjavik for the road trip to save money.
meals.dinner: Dine at Rauðka Restaurant in Siglufjörður — a cozy local spot serving Icelandic fish dishes and lamb. Expect to spend around 3,500–5,000 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Keflavik to Siglufjörður is approximately 380 km and takes 5–6 hours. Check road conditions at road.is before departing. January roads in northern Iceland can be icy — a 4WD vehicle is strongly recommended. Arrive before dark if possible as mountain roads can be treacherous at night.

day_by_day.morning: After a good night's rest, enjoy a leisurely morning exploring Siglufjörður. Visit the award-winning Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið) — one of Iceland's best regional museums, showcasing the town's rich herring fishing history. Open from 10:00.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or walk to the nearby Héðinsfjörður valley, an abandoned fjord settlement accessible via a short tunnel. Explore the hauntingly beautiful landscape and old farmstead ruins. Return to town and warm up with a hot drink at a local café.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights watch from the harbor or a short drive out of town toward Héðinsfjörður for darker skies. Check aurora forecast at en.vedur.is. If clouds obscure the view, enjoy a relaxed evening at the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Hotel Siglunes (included if offered) or pick up fresh pastries and coffee at a local bakery.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Kaffi Rauðka or grab a bowl of lamb soup at a local café — budget around 2,000–3,000 ISK.
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal using groceries from the local Samkaup store in Siglufjörður to save on budget, or dine again at Rauðka for fresh catch of the day.

day_by_day.notes: January sunrise in Siglufjörður is around 11:00 and sunset around 15:30 — daylight is very limited. Plan outdoor activities between 10:00 and 15:00. Dress in thermal layers, waterproof outer shell, and sturdy boots.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south along the scenic Tröllaskagi peninsula (Route 76 and Route 82) toward Akureyri, Iceland's 'Capital of the North' (approx. 1.5 hours). Explore the charming town center, visit the Akureyri Botanical Garden (free entry), and browse local shops on Hafnarstræti.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the iconic Akureyrarkirkja church perched on a hill overlooking the town — stunning even in winter. Explore the Akureyri Art Museum or the Nonni House museum. Stroll along the fjord waterfront.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður before dark (depart Akureyri by 14:30 at the latest). Spend the evening watching for Northern Lights from the hotel or a nearby dark spot. Check aurora alerts on the Vedur app.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Hotel Siglunes before departing.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Akureyri at Strikið Restaurant or Bautinn — try the Icelandic lamb burger or fish and chips. Budget 2,500–4,000 ISK.
meals.dinner: Pick up groceries in Akureyri (larger supermarket selection than Siglufjörður) and prepare a simple dinner at the hotel, or dine at Rauðka upon return.

day_by_day.notes: Akureyri is approximately 75 km from Siglufjörður. The drive is scenic but can be slow in winter conditions. Fill up your fuel tank in Akureyri as fuel stations are sparse in the north. Akureyri has a Bónus supermarket for affordable grocery shopping.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Lake Mývatn area (approx. 1 hour east of Akureyri, 1.5 hours from Siglufjörður). Start with the Mývatn Nature Baths — a less crowded and more affordable alternative to the Blue Lagoon, with geothermal pools set against a dramatic volcanic landscape. Open from 09:00.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Mývatn volcanic landscape: visit Dimmuborgir lava formations, Hverfjall crater (if accessible in winter), and the Skútustaðagígar pseudocraters. The eerie black lava fields are otherworldly in winter light.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Siglufjörður. The Mývatn area is known for excellent Northern Lights viewing — if the forecast is good, consider staying until dark before heading back. Alternatively, watch from the road on the return journey.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Hotel Siglunes before the drive.
meals.lunch: Café at Mývatn Nature Baths or Vogafjós Farm Restaurant near Mývatn — try the fresh skyr and geothermal bread. Budget 2,500–3,500 ISK.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Hotel Siglunes restaurant or Rauðka upon return to Siglufjörður.

day_by_day.notes: Mývatn Nature Baths entry is approximately 5,500 ISK per adult — more affordable than the Blue Lagoon. Bring a swimsuit and towel. The drive from Siglufjörður to Mývatn passes through Akureyri — allow 1.5–2 hours each way in winter. Check road conditions carefully.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the area around Siglufjörður on foot. Hike the lower slopes of the mountains surrounding the town (stay on marked paths and avoid avalanche zones — check with locals). The views over the fjord are spectacular even in winter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Siglufjörður Folk Museum or spend time at the local swimming pool (sundlaug) — a beloved Icelandic tradition. The geothermally heated outdoor pool is perfect for warming up on a cold January day. Entry is very affordable (approx. 1,000 ISK).
day_by_day.evening: Dedicated Northern Lights hunting evening. Drive 5–10 minutes out of town toward Héðinsfjörður tunnel for darker skies. Bring a thermos of hot chocolate, a tripod for photography, and warm blankets. Stay out for 1–2 hours if the aurora forecast is favorable (KP index 2+).

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Hotel Siglunes.
meals.lunch: Homemade packed lunch or soup at a local café in Siglufjörður.
meals.dinner: Try cooking an Icelandic-inspired meal at the hotel if kitchen facilities are available — pick up skyr, smoked lamb (hangikjöt), and rye bread from the local store.

day_by_day.notes: January is prime Northern Lights season in northern Iceland. Siglufjörður's location at 66°N (just above the Arctic Circle) gives excellent aurora viewing potential. Download the Vedur aurora forecast app and set alerts for KP index 3+. Clear skies are the key variable — cloud cover is the main obstacle.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Hofsós (approx. 45 minutes south of Siglufjörður). Visit the Icelandic Emigration Center, which tells the fascinating story of Icelanders who emigrated to North America. Also visit the stunning infinity-edge geothermal swimming pool at Hofsós — one of Iceland's most scenic pools, overlooking the fjord.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Sauðárkrókur (approx. 30 minutes from Hofsós), the largest town in the Skagafjörður region. Explore the town, visit the local museum, and browse the shops. The Skagafjörður area is famous for Icelandic horses — look out for herds in the fields.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður via the scenic coastal route. Stop at a viewpoint along the way for Northern Lights watching if skies are clear.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Hotel Siglunes.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Hofsós swimming pool café or a local restaurant in Sauðárkrókur — try the fish soup. Budget 2,000–3,000 ISK.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Rauðka in Siglufjörður or a self-catered meal at the hotel.

day_by_day.notes: The Hofsós geothermal pool (Sundlaug Hofsóss) is one of Iceland's hidden gems — entry is around 1,000 ISK. Bring a swimsuit. The pool may have limited winter hours — call ahead to confirm opening times. The drive along Skagafjörður offers beautiful winter scenery.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and relaxation day in Siglufjörður. Sleep in, enjoy a slow breakfast, and spend the morning reading or exploring the town at a leisurely pace. Visit the local harbor and watch fishing boats come and go.
day_by_day.afternoon: Attend a guided Northern Lights Hunting Tour departing from the Akureyri area (book in advance). Many tour operators pick up from Akureyri — drive there (1.5 hours) to join the tour. These guided tours use cloud-chasing vehicles to find clear skies and optimal aurora viewing spots.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunting Tour continues into the evening (typically 21:00–00:00). Expert guides explain the science of the aurora and help with photography. Return to Siglufjörður late evening.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at Hotel Siglunes.
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Siglufjörður before driving to Akureyri.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Akureyri before the tour — try Strikið for a mid-range Icelandic meal (3,500–5,500 ISK) or grab a burger at Hamborgarabúlla Tómasar.

day_by_day.notes: Northern Lights tours from Akureyri typically cost 8,000–12,000 ISK per person. Book well in advance for January as tours fill up quickly. Most reputable operators offer a 'come again free' policy if no lights are seen. Recommended operators: Arctic Adventures, Saga Travel, or local Akureyri-based guides.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the drive south toward the Golden Circle and Reykjavik area (this is a long travel day — approximately 5–6 hours). Depart Siglufjörður early. Drive via Akureyri and south on Route 1.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at Goðafoss waterfall (approx. 50 km east of Akureyri) — one of Iceland's most spectacular waterfalls, especially dramatic in winter with ice formations. Continue south, stopping at Hveravellir geothermal area if road conditions permit (F-road — check carefully in January).
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in the South Iceland / Selfoss area or continue to Reykjavik. Check into a guesthouse or budget hotel in the Selfoss area as a base for the next few days. Alternatively, stay in Reykjavik for better dining and amenity options.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Hotel Siglunes before checkout.
meals.lunch: Stop at a roadside restaurant or N1 petrol station café along Route 1 — Icelandic petrol station food is surprisingly good and affordable (1,500–2,500 ISK).
meals.dinner: Dinner at a restaurant in Selfoss or Reykjavik — try Tryggvaskáli in Selfoss for traditional Icelandic cuisine at mid-range prices.

day_by_day.notes: This is the longest driving day of the trip. Depart by 08:00 to arrive before dark. The Hveravellir F-road (F35) is almost certainly closed in January — do not attempt it. Stick to Route 1 (Ring Road) which is maintained year-round. Check road.is before departing. Consider booking accommodation in Selfoss or Hveragerði for proximity to the Secret Lagoon.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring in Flúðir (approx. 1 hour from Selfoss). Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool dating back to 1891 — a natural hot spring surrounded by geysers and steaming vents. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon and more authentic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Golden Circle: visit Þingvellir National Park (UNESCO World Heritage Site) where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet. Walk through the dramatic Almannagjá gorge. Then visit the Geysir geothermal area to watch Strokkur erupt every 5–10 minutes.
day_by_day.evening: Complete the Golden Circle with a visit to Gullfoss waterfall — stunning in winter with ice and snow. Return to accommodation. Check aurora forecast for evening Northern Lights viewing from Þingvellir or a rural area.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at accommodation.
meals.lunch: Café at the Secret Lagoon or the Geysir Center café — try the lamb soup and fresh bread. Budget 2,500–3,500 ISK.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Lindin Restaurant in Laugarvatn (near the Golden Circle) — excellent local cuisine in a cozy setting. Budget 4,000–6,000 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: Secret Lagoon entry is approximately 3,500 ISK per adult — book online in advance. Bring a swimsuit and towel. The Golden Circle is Iceland's most popular tourist route — even in January it can be busy on weekends. Þingvellir is free to enter (parking fee applies). Gullfoss is free.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to the South Coast. Visit Seljalandsfoss waterfall (you can walk behind it — may be icy/closed in January, check conditions) and Skógafoss waterfall. Both are dramatic and photogenic in winter with ice formations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue east to Reynisfjara black sand beach near Vík — one of the world's most dramatic beaches with towering basalt columns and powerful Atlantic waves. Exercise extreme caution with sneaker waves. Visit the Reynisdrangar sea stacks.
day_by_day.evening: Return west toward accommodation. Stop at Dyrhólaey promontory for panoramic views if daylight permits. Evening Northern Lights watch from a dark rural area on the South Coast — the flat landscape offers excellent 360° sky views.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at accommodation.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Skógarfoss Café or a restaurant in Vík — try the fish and chips or lamb stew. Budget 2,500–4,000 ISK.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Suður-Vík Restaurant in Vík or drive back to Selfoss area for dinner. Budget 3,500–5,000 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: Reynisfjara beach is extremely dangerous — never turn your back on the ocean. Sneaker waves have killed tourists here. Stay well back from the water. Seljalandsfoss walkway behind the waterfall is often closed in winter due to ice — check locally. The South Coast drive is approximately 2–3 hours from Selfoss.

day_by_day.morning: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa experience (pre-booked). Drive to the Reykjanes Peninsula (approx. 45 minutes from Reykjavik). Soak in the iconic milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy the in-water bar, silica mud mask, and steam caves. Book the Comfort package for a mid-range experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Reykjanes Peninsula after the Blue Lagoon. Visit the Bridge Between Continents (walk between tectonic plates), the Gunnuhver hot spring area, and the Reykjanesviti lighthouse. The volcanic landscape is dramatic and otherworldly.
day_by_day.evening: Drive to Reykjavik (30 minutes from Reykjanes). Explore the capital city in the evening — walk along Laugavegur shopping street, visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church (lit up beautifully at night), and enjoy Reykjavik's vibrant dining scene.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before driving to Blue Lagoon (opens at 08:00 in January).
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Blue Lagoon's LAVA Restaurant or the more affordable Lagoon Bar — budget 3,000–5,000 ISK for a light meal.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Reykjavik — try Messinn for excellent fish dishes at mid-range prices (4,000–6,000 ISK) or Sægreifinn (Sea Baron) for famous lobster soup at a very affordable price (around 1,800 ISK per bowl).

day_by_day.notes: Blue Lagoon MUST be booked well in advance — January slots sell out weeks ahead. Comfort package costs approximately 14,990 ISK and includes towel, one drink, and silica mud mask. Arrive at your booked time slot. The Blue Lagoon is located near Keflavik Airport — convenient for the final days of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Reykjavik. Visit Hallgrímskirkja church and take the elevator to the top for panoramic city views. Walk to the Harpa Concert Hall on the waterfront — stunning glass architecture. Visit the National Museum of Iceland for an excellent overview of Icelandic history and culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Perlan museum — a stunning glass dome building with exhibits on Iceland's natural wonders including a real ice cave tunnel, Northern Lights planetarium show, and glacier exhibit. Excellent for understanding Iceland's geology and nature. Then stroll through the old harbor area.
day_by_day.evening: Final Northern Lights attempt — join a Northern Lights boat tour from Reykjavik harbor (a unique perspective from the water) or take a bus tour to dark areas outside the city. Alternatively, drive 30 minutes out of Reykjavik to Þingvellir for dark sky viewing.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Reykjavik accommodation or at Brauð & Co bakery — famous for their cinnamon rolls and sourdough (budget 1,500–2,000 ISK).
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café Loki near Hallgrímskirkja — try the traditional Icelandic rye bread with smoked salmon and skyr. Budget 2,500–3,500 ISK.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Grillmarkaðurinn (Grill Market) — one of Reykjavik's best restaurants for Icelandic ingredients cooked over lava stone grill. Budget 6,000–9,000 ISK per person for a special meal.

day_by_day.notes: Perlan museum entry is approximately 4,990 ISK and is highly recommended. The Northern Lights boat tour from Reykjavik harbor costs approximately 9,900 ISK — book in advance. Reykjavik's light pollution makes city-based aurora viewing difficult; getting outside the city is essential for good views.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. If your flight departs in the afternoon, use the morning for last-minute shopping on Laugavegur street — pick up Icelandic wool sweaters (lopapeysa), local chocolates, skyr, and other souvenirs. Visit the Kolaportið flea market if open (weekends only — check schedule).
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Keflavik International Airport (45 minutes from Reykjavik). Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for check-in and security. Return rental car. Enjoy a final Icelandic meal at the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Keflavik International Airport. Reflect on 13 incredible days of Northern Lights, hot springs, dramatic landscapes, and Icelandic culture.

meals.breakfast: Final Icelandic breakfast — try skyr with berries, smoked salmon on rye bread, and strong Icelandic coffee at a Reykjavik café.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Keflavik Airport or grab a final bowl of lamb soup before heading to the airport.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal.

day_by_day.notes: Check flight departure time carefully and plan the airport drive accordingly. Keflavik Airport is 50 km from Reykjavik city center — allow 45–60 minutes driving time plus extra for winter road conditions. Return the rental car with a full tank of fuel (there are petrol stations near the airport). Duty-free shopping at Keflavik is excellent — Icelandic spirits, chocolate, and skincare products make great gifts.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Iceland Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunting Tour
experiences.description: Join a guided evening tour away from Reykjavik's light pollution to witness the Aurora Borealis dancing across the sky. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and you'll learn about the science behind this natural phenomenon while capturing stunning photographs.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, silica mud masks, and steam caves while surrounded by dramatic lava fields. Book the Comfort package for access to the lagoon, a silica mud mask, and a drink at the in-water bar.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring dating back to 1891 surrounded by geothermal activity, bubbling geysers, and a small waterfall. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic experience offers a more intimate connection with Iceland's geothermal landscape.

experiences.name: Vatnajökull Glacier Hike
experiences.description: Strap on crampons and explore the largest glacier in Europe with a certified glacier guide. Trek across stunning ice formations, peer into brilliant blue crevasses, and learn about Iceland's rapidly changing glacial landscape. This guided hike offers an unforgettable encounter with Iceland's raw natural power.

experiences.name: Landmannalaugar Highland Hot Springs Trek
experiences.description: Hike through Iceland's surreal rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains in the Highlands and reward yourself with a soak in natural geothermal hot springs at the base camp. The vivid landscape of red, green, yellow, and purple volcanic rock is unlike anywhere else on Earth, making this a bucket-list nature experience.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Keflavík International Airport at 06:10. Clear customs and collect luggage. Arrange private luxury transfer (pre-booked Mercedes V-Class or similar) to begin the scenic drive north toward Siglufjörður. Stop at the Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa en route — enjoy a premium 'Retreat' package with in-water massage, silica mud mask, algae mask, and a glass of sparkling wine in the milky-blue geothermal waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the private transfer northward through the Snæfellsnes Peninsula and along the dramatic fjord roads. Stop at Varmahlíð for a warm lunch break. Arrive at Hotel Siglunes in Siglufjörður by late afternoon. Check in, settle into your luxury room, and take in the breathtaking fjord views from the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Freshen up and enjoy a welcome dinner at the hotel's acclaimed restaurant, sampling locally sourced Arctic char, lamb, and Icelandic seafood. Afterward, step outside or join a short guided walk along the fjord waterfront to scan the skies for the Northern Lights — January darkness and Siglufjörður's minimal light pollution make it an excellent vantage point.

meals.breakfast: Light refreshments at Keflavík Airport lounge (Saga Lounge if flying Business) or grab-and-go from airport café upon arrival
meals.lunch: Á Naustið or Hótel Varmahlíð restaurant in Varmahlíð — hearty Icelandic lamb soup and fresh bread
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes restaurant — multi-course tasting menu featuring pan-seared Arctic char, slow-roasted Icelandic lamb, and skyr-based dessert with local berry compote; pair with Icelandic craft beer or curated wine list

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the Blue Lagoon Retreat Spa package well in advance as January slots fill quickly. Ensure private transfer is arranged before departure. Pack warm layers accessible in carry-on for the cold January temperatures (avg. 5°C). Drive from Blue Lagoon to Siglufjörður is approximately 4–4.5 hours; road conditions may vary — confirm with transfer driver.

day_by_day.morning: After a leisurely breakfast at Hotel Siglunes, take a guided walking tour of Siglufjörður town — explore the charming colorful harbor, the famous Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið), and learn about the town's rich fishing heritage. The museum is one of Iceland's finest and offers fascinating insight into the 20th-century herring boom.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or arrange a private guided excursion along the Tröllaskagi Peninsula. Visit the dramatic Héðinsfjörður — an abandoned fjord accessible through the Héðinsfjörður tunnel — and explore the hauntingly beautiful deserted farmsteads surrounded by towering snow-dusted mountains. Photography opportunities are exceptional in the low winter light.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður for a Northern Lights Hunting Tour. A local expert guide will take you by 4WD vehicle to optimal dark-sky locations around the fjords and mountain ridges above town, away from any ambient light. Wrap up in provided thermal suits and enjoy hot cocoa while watching for the Aurora Borealis dancing overhead.

meals.breakfast: Full Icelandic breakfast at Hotel Siglunes — skyr with berries, smoked salmon, rye bread, eggs, and Icelandic dairy
meals.lunch: Kaffi Rauðka in Siglufjörður — cozy café with homemade soups, open-faced sandwiches, and freshly baked pastries
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes restaurant — pan-seared cod with butter sauce and root vegetables, followed by Icelandic cheese board and local schnapps

day_by_day.notes: Northern Lights visibility depends on clear skies and solar activity. Check the Icelandic Met Office aurora forecast (vedur.is) each evening. January offers up to 18+ hours of darkness, maximizing aurora viewing windows. Dress in multiple thermal layers; temperatures near the fjord at night can feel significantly colder with wind chill.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a relaxed morning breakfast at the hotel. Take a scenic snowshoe or winter hiking excursion on the lower slopes above Siglufjörður with a private mountain guide. The views over the fjord and surrounding peaks in the crisp January morning light are spectacular. Spot local birdlife including ptarmigan and ravens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive south along Route 76 to Hofsós, a picturesque village on the Skagafjörður fjord. Visit the Hofsós Infinity Pool — a geothermal swimming pool dramatically perched on the fjord's edge with panoramic views of the water and mountains. Soak in the warm geothermal waters while surrounded by Iceland's raw winter landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður. Enjoy a private in-hotel Northern Lights alert service — the hotel staff will notify you if the aurora becomes visible. Spend the evening in the hotel's lounge with a glass of Icelandic gin or whisky, then head outside when conditions are favorable for aurora viewing directly from the hotel terrace.

meals.breakfast: Full Icelandic breakfast at Hotel Siglunes
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch prepared by Hotel Siglunes kitchen — thermos of soup, artisan sandwiches, and Icelandic chocolate for the snowshoe excursion
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes — slow-braised Icelandic lamb shank with root vegetable purée, followed by warm skyr cake with crowberry sauce

day_by_day.notes: Hofsós Infinity Pool is approximately 45 minutes from Siglufjörður. Bring swimwear and a towel (or rent on-site). The pool is heated to around 38–40°C — a magical contrast to the cold winter air. Road conditions on Route 76 in January can be icy; use a 4WD vehicle and check road.is before departing.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided day trip south toward Akureyri — Iceland's 'Capital of the North.' Depart after breakfast and drive the scenic Route 82 along the Eyjafjörður fjord. Arrive in Akureyri and explore the charming town center, including the iconic Akureyrarkirkja church perched on the hillside with sweeping fjord views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Akureyri Botanical Garden (Lystigarðurinn) — the world's northernmost botanical garden — then explore the boutique shops and galleries along Hafnarstræti. Stop at the Geosea Geothermal Sea Baths just outside Húsavík (if extending the day trip) or enjoy a private spa treatment at Hotel Kea's wellness facilities in Akureyri.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at one of Akureyri's finest restaurants before returning to Siglufjörður by private transfer. Keep eyes open for Northern Lights on the drive back along the dark fjord roads — this route is particularly spectacular for aurora viewing.

meals.breakfast: Full Icelandic breakfast at Hotel Siglunes before departure
meals.lunch: Rub23 Restaurant in Akureyri — acclaimed for its sushi and Icelandic seafood fusion; try the Arctic char sashimi and langoustine
meals.dinner: Strikið Restaurant in Akureyri — rooftop dining with panoramic fjord views; signature dishes include pan-fried monkfish and Icelandic beef tenderloin

day_by_day.notes: Akureyri is approximately 75 km from Siglufjörður (about 1.5 hours drive). A private driver is recommended for this day trip to allow full flexibility and safety on winter roads. Akureyri is a wonderful small city with a surprisingly vibrant food and arts scene for its size.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated Northern Lights morning recovery and leisure day. Sleep in and enjoy a late, indulgent breakfast at the hotel. Spend the morning in the hotel's cozy lounge reading, journaling, or enjoying the fjord views from your room. Optional: book an in-room spa treatment or massage through the hotel's concierge service.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Siglufjörður's local culture more deeply — visit the Folk Music Centre (Þjóðlagasetur) to experience traditional Icelandic music and instruments. Walk along the harbor to watch local fishing boats and chat with fishermen. Browse the small local shops for Icelandic wool products (lopapeysa sweaters) and artisan crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Premium Northern Lights Hunting Tour with a specialist aurora guide. Travel by luxury 4WD to multiple pre-scouted dark-sky locations in the mountains above the fjord. The guide will use real-time aurora forecasting apps and cloud cover maps to maximize your chances. Hot drinks, thermal blankets, and a tripod for photography provided.

meals.breakfast: Extended late breakfast at Hotel Siglunes — eggs Benedict with smoked salmon, fresh pastries, and Icelandic coffee
meals.lunch: Sægreifinn (The Sea Baron) style — visit a local Siglufjörður fish market or café for fresh langoustine soup and grilled fish
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes — chef's special tasting menu with wine pairing; expect seasonal ingredients including reindeer, Arctic char, and foraged herbs

day_by_day.notes: January 20th statistically offers good aurora probability if skies are clear. The Kp index forecast should be checked at spaceweather.com or the Icelandic Met Office. A rest day mid-trip helps combat travel fatigue and ensures you're alert for evening aurora hunting.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided excursion to the Skagafjörður region — one of Iceland's most dramatic and historically rich fjords. Visit Glaumbær Turf Farm Museum, a beautifully preserved 18th-century turf farmhouse complex that offers a vivid window into traditional Icelandic rural life. The snow-covered turf roofs in winter are extraordinarily photogenic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Varmahlíð area for horse riding with Icelandic horses — the unique tölt gait makes for a smooth, comfortable ride even for beginners. A private guided ride through the snow-dusted Skagafjörður landscape is an unforgettable experience. Icelandic horses are famously friendly and hardy.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður. Enjoy a quiet evening at the hotel with a private in-room dining experience — arrange with the hotel concierge for a romantic or exclusive dinner served in your room or a private dining space with fjord views. Watch for Northern Lights from your window or the hotel terrace.

meals.breakfast: Full Icelandic breakfast at Hotel Siglunes
meals.lunch: Hótel Varmahlíð restaurant — traditional Icelandic lamb stew (kjötsúpa) with freshly baked rye bread and butter
meals.dinner: Private in-room dining at Hotel Siglunes — curated menu by the chef featuring local delicacies, with a bottle of premium Icelandic or Scandinavian wine

day_by_day.notes: Horse riding in January requires appropriate warm clothing — the stables will provide helmets and may offer riding suits. Glaumbær Museum may have limited winter hours; confirm opening times in advance. Skagafjörður is renowned as Iceland's horse capital — the quality of horses and guides here is exceptional.

day_by_day.morning: Extended day trip to the Mývatn region — one of Iceland's most geologically active and visually stunning areas. Depart early after breakfast for the approximately 2-hour drive east. First stop: Goðafoss Waterfall — the 'Waterfall of the Gods' — dramatic even in winter with ice formations framing the cascading water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Lake Mývatn. Visit the Mývatn Nature Baths — a premium geothermal lagoon experience similar to the Blue Lagoon but far less crowded and arguably more naturally beautiful. Soak in the mineral-rich alkaline waters at 36–40°C while surrounded by volcanic landscapes. Also explore the surreal Dimmuborgir lava formations and Hverfjall volcanic crater.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in the Mývatn area before the scenic drive back to Siglufjörður. The return journey through the dark Icelandic highlands offers prime Northern Lights viewing — ask your driver to stop at optimal locations if the aurora appears.

meals.breakfast: Full Icelandic breakfast at Hotel Siglunes before early departure
meals.lunch: Vogafjós Farm Restaurant at Lake Mývatn — famous for its geothermally baked rye bread, fresh dairy, and farm-to-table Icelandic cuisine
meals.dinner: Gamli Bærinn (The Old Farm) restaurant near Mývatn — cozy atmosphere with hearty Icelandic dishes including lamb and freshwater fish from the lake

day_by_day.notes: Mývatn Nature Baths should be pre-booked. The drive from Siglufjörður to Mývatn is approximately 2 hours each way — a private driver is essential. Road conditions on Route 1 (Ring Road) in January can be challenging; always check road.is. This is a long day — depart by 8:00 AM to maximize time at Mývatn.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning after the long Mývatn day. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast and a slow morning at the hotel. Optional: arrange a private yoga or meditation session in the hotel's quiet lounge space overlooking the fjord — a deeply restorative experience in this serene Arctic setting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Siglufjörður area on a private guided photography tour. A local photographer guide will take you to the most scenic winter vantage points around the fjord — frozen waterfalls, snow-laden mountain slopes, colorful harbor reflections, and the dramatic tunnel entrances. Perfect for capturing the essence of this remote Arctic town.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunting Tour — second dedicated aurora excursion. Travel to a different set of dark-sky locations than the first tour, including elevated mountain viewpoints above the fjord. The guide will set up a bonfire or provide a heated shelter for comfort during the wait. Hot chocolate and Icelandic schnapps provided.

meals.breakfast: Extended breakfast at Hotel Siglunes — smoked lamb, skyr parfait, fresh waffles with Icelandic butter and jam
meals.lunch: Kaffi Rauðka in Siglufjörður — homemade fish soup, freshly baked bread, and a slice of traditional Icelandic cake
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes — special Saturday evening menu; expect a premium seafood platter featuring langoustine, scallops, and smoked salmon, followed by Icelandic lamb and a decadent dessert

day_by_day.notes: January 23rd falls on a Saturday — the hotel may have special weekend programming. The photography tour is best arranged through the hotel concierge with a local guide who knows the area intimately. Bring or rent a tripod for long-exposure aurora photography.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Snæfellsnes Peninsula — one of Iceland's most diverse and dramatic landscapes. Depart early for the long but scenic drive south and west. Visit the iconic Kirkjufell mountain and Kirkjufellsfoss waterfall — arguably Iceland's most photographed landscape, especially magical in winter snow.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the Snæfellsnes Peninsula to Snæfellsjökull National Park. The glacier-capped volcano (immortalized in Jules Verne's 'Journey to the Centre of the Earth') dominates the landscape. Explore the dramatic lava fields, sea cliffs, and black sand beaches of Djúpalónssandur. Visit the charming fishing village of Arnarstapi.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the return drive to Siglufjörður, stopping for dinner in Borgarnes or Blönduós. The long drive back through the dark Icelandic countryside offers excellent aurora viewing opportunities — ask your driver to monitor conditions and stop if the lights appear.

meals.breakfast: Early full breakfast at Hotel Siglunes before departure
meals.lunch: Picnic-style gourmet packed lunch from Hotel Siglunes kitchen — enjoyed with views of Kirkjufell mountain
meals.dinner: Settlement Center Restaurant (Landnámssetur) in Borgarnes — excellent Icelandic cuisine in a historic setting; try the lamb and langoustine dishes

day_by_day.notes: This is a very long day trip (Snæfellsnes is approximately 3.5–4 hours from Siglufjörður). Consider whether to break the journey with an overnight in Snæfellsnes or Borgarnes — discuss with your travel concierge. A private driver is essential. Snæfellsjökull glacier tours are not recommended in January without specialist guides.

day_by_day.morning: Recovery day after the long Snæfellsnes excursion. Sleep in and enjoy a late breakfast. Spend the morning at leisure — read in the hotel lounge, enjoy the fjord views, or arrange an in-hotel spa treatment. The hotel's peaceful atmosphere and stunning location make it a destination in itself.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring — Iceland's oldest swimming pool, dating to 1891. Located in Flúðir in the South Iceland highlands, this requires a longer drive, but the experience of soaking in a naturally bubbling hot spring surrounded by geothermal activity and snow-covered fields is uniquely authentic and far less commercialized than the Blue Lagoon. Note: this may be combined with a future day trip south.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður for a final evening aurora hunt. By now you'll know the best local spots — take a self-guided walk to your favorite dark-sky location near the hotel, or join the hotel's informal aurora alert network. Celebrate any sightings with a glass of Icelandic aquavit at the hotel bar.

meals.breakfast: Late, indulgent breakfast at Hotel Siglunes — full spread with all Icelandic specialties
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the hotel — Icelandic fish cakes, salad, and fresh bread
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes — chef's choice seasonal menu; request a special dietary preference or celebration menu if desired

day_by_day.notes: The Secret Lagoon in Flúðir is approximately 4 hours from Siglufjörður — this activity may be better suited to a day when you're traveling south toward Reykjavík. Consider rescheduling this experience to Day 12 or 13 if the itinerary allows. Alternatively, enjoy the Hofsós pool again as a closer alternative.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided ice fishing experience on a frozen lake near Siglufjörður or in the Skagafjörður region. A local guide will drill holes in the ice and teach you traditional Icelandic ice fishing techniques. This quintessential Arctic winter activity is both meditative and exciting — Arctic char and trout are common catches.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Tröllaskagi Brewery in Siglufjörður — one of Iceland's most acclaimed craft breweries, producing exceptional beers using pure Icelandic water and local ingredients. Enjoy a private guided tasting session of their seasonal winter ales, stouts, and lagers. The brewery's location in this remote fjord town adds to its charm.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at Hotel Siglunes — request the chef's grand tasting menu with full wine pairing as a celebration of your time in Siglufjörður. After dinner, take one final walk along the fjord waterfront under the stars, hoping for a farewell aurora display.

meals.breakfast: Full Icelandic breakfast at Hotel Siglunes
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Tröllaskagi Brewery — brewery snacks, charcuterie, and Icelandic cheeses paired with craft beers
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes — grand farewell tasting menu: langoustine bisque, smoked Arctic char, Icelandic lamb rack, artisan cheese course, and skyr panna cotta with crowberry coulis; full wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Ice fishing requires warm, waterproof clothing and patience — the guide will provide all necessary equipment. Tröllaskagi Brewery is a genuine highlight of Siglufjörður and should not be missed. Book the brewery tasting in advance as private sessions may require prior arrangement.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of Hotel Siglunes after a final breakfast. Begin the private transfer south toward Reykjavík, taking the scenic coastal route. Stop at Blönduós for a coffee break and to admire the Blanda River estuary. Continue south through the dramatic Holtavörðuheiði highland plateau.
day_by_day.afternoon: Detour to Flúðir to visit the Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring — Iceland's oldest swimming pool (1891). Soak in the naturally bubbling geothermal pool surrounded by steaming hot springs, geysers, and snow-covered fields. This intimate, authentic experience is a perfect contrast to the Blue Lagoon visited on Day 1. Afterward, continue toward Reykjavík.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Reykjavík and check into a luxury hotel (The Retreat at Blue Lagoon, Hotel Borg, or ION Adventure Hotel recommended). Freshen up and enjoy dinner at one of Reykjavík's finest restaurants — the city's culinary scene is world-class.

meals.breakfast: Final full breakfast at Hotel Siglunes
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch from Hotel Siglunes for the road, or stop at Hótel Varmahlíð for a warm meal
meals.dinner: Dill Restaurant in Reykjavík — Iceland's first Michelin-starred restaurant, offering a stunning Nordic tasting menu with Icelandic ingredients; advance reservation essential

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Siglufjörður to Reykjavík via Flúðir is approximately 5–6 hours including stops. Pre-book the Secret Lagoon and Reykjavík luxury hotel well in advance. If staying at The Retreat at Blue Lagoon, dinner can be taken at their acclaimed Moss Restaurant instead of Dill.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. Enjoy a luxurious breakfast at your Reykjavík hotel. If time permits, take a morning walk along Reykjavík's Sæbraut waterfront promenade to the iconic Harpa Concert Hall — stunning in the winter morning light. Browse the boutiques on Laugavegur street for last-minute Icelandic gifts: lopapeysa wool sweaters, Icelandic sea salt, craft spirits, and local design.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, visit the Perlan Museum — a stunning glass-domed building with a 360° viewing deck and immersive exhibitions on Iceland's natural wonders including glaciers, volcanoes, and the Northern Lights. Alternatively, enjoy a final soak at Laugardalslaug — Reykjavík's largest geothermal swimming complex — a beloved local experience.
day_by_day.evening: Private luxury transfer to Keflavík International Airport. Arrive with ample time for check-in and enjoy the Saga Lounge (Business Class) before your departure flight. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of Northern Lights, geothermal wonders, dramatic landscapes, and the unique magic of Iceland in winter.

meals.breakfast: Luxury hotel breakfast in Reykjavík — full spread with Icelandic specialties, fresh pastries, and premium coffee
meals.lunch: Grillmarkaðurinn (The Grill Market) in Reykjavík — premium Icelandic steakhouse with exceptional local beef, lamb, and seafood; perfect for a final Icelandic feast
meals.dinner: Light dining at Keflavík Airport Saga Lounge or onboard Icelandair flight

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure flight time and arrange airport transfer accordingly — allow at least 2.5 hours before departure for international flights from Keflavík. Duty-free at Keflavík is excellent for Icelandic spirits (Brennivín, Flóki Whisky), Nói Síríus chocolate, and skincare products. Ensure all Northern Lights photos are backed up before departure!
